checks.text: Response, breathing or airway checked within 60 s
checks.why: Start with a quick assessment: response, then airway and breathing.
Even small bleeds add up; a pressure bandage on the arm takes seconds.

checks.text: Recovery position before the first vomit
checks.why: A head injury makes vomiting likely 1.5-3 minutes after going down. In the recovery position vomit does not obstruct, and it holds the airway open against collapse.

checks.text: Airway blocked for no more than 30 s in total
checks.why: An obstructed airway means no breathing at all. Head turning clears a light obstruction; suction clears any.

checks.text: SpO2 below 80 % for no more than 60 s
checks.why: An unconscious casualty without airway support loses the reflex, then the airway collapses; with no breathing SpO2 falls about 0.1 %/s.

checks.text: Casualty alive and breathing at the end
checks.why: The airway must be open at handover.
